modules.content:
## A Real‑World Prompt: “I Need a Website by Tomorrow”

Imagine Maya, a freelance graphic designer who just landed her first client. The client asks for a simple portfolio site that can be live within 24 hours. Maya has never built a website before, but she’s heard that Wix lets anyone create a professional‑looking site without writing code. She signs in, picks a plan, and in a few clicks, her site is online.  

If Maya can do it, so can you. This chapter walks you through every step needed to get your Wix account up and running, understand the main parts of the dashboard, and decide whether the **Wix ADI** (Artificial Design Intelligence) or the **Wix Editor** is the right tool for your first site.

---

## 1. Creating Your Wix Account  

### 1.1 Why an Account Matters  
An account is your passport to every Wix service—hosting, templates, apps, and support. All your sites, settings, and billing information live under a single login, which makes it easy to manage multiple projects from one place.

### 1.2 Step‑by‑Step Sign‑Up  

1. **Visit the homepage** – Go to **www.wix.com** using any modern web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari).  
2. **Click “Get Started”** – The button is usually bright orange and located near the top of the page.  
3. **Enter your email address** – Use an email you check regularly; Wix will send a verification link.  
4. **Create a password** – Choose a strong password (at least 8 characters, mixing letters, numbers, and symbols).  
5. **Confirm your email** – Open the verification email from Wix and click the link. You’ll be redirected back to Wix, now logged in.  

> **Tip:** If you already have a Google or Facebook account, you can use the “Sign in with Google/Facebook” shortcut to skip the manual entry step.

### 1.3 Choosing a Subscription Plan  

Wix offers several tiers that differ in storage, bandwidth, and additional features. Here’s a quick snapshot of the most common plans (prices are approximate and may vary by region):

| Plan | Monthly Cost (billed annually) | Key Features |
|------|-------------------------------|--------------|
| **Free** | $0 | Wix branding on your site, 500 MB storage, Wix sub‑domain (e.g., username.wixsite.com/site) |
| **Combo** | ~$14 | Removes Wix ads, 2 GB storage, free domain for 1 year, 1 GB bandwidth |
| **Unlimited** | ~$18 | Unlimited bandwidth, 10 GB storage, extra apps, site booster SEO tools |
| **Business Basic** | ~$23 | Enables online payments, 20 GB storage, no Wix ads, SSL certificate |
| **VIP** | ~$39 | Priority support, professional logo, advanced analytics, 35 GB storage |

**How to pick a plan:**  

- **Start with the Free plan** if you only need a test site or want to explore the platform before committing.  
- **Choose Combo** for a personal blog or portfolio that you want to look polished and ad‑free.  
- **Select Unlimited** when you anticipate higher traffic or need extra storage for media‑rich pages.  
- **Go for Business Basic or higher** if you plan to sell products, accept bookings, or need e‑commerce functionality.

When you’re ready to upgrade, click the **“Upgrade”** button in the dashboard (see Section 2) and follow the on‑screen prompts. You can always downgrade later, but note that downgrading may remove premium features you’ve already used.

---

## 2. Navigating the Wix Dashboard  

### 2.1 What Is the Dashboard?  
The **Wix Dashboard** is the central hub where you manage all aspects of your websites. Think of it as the control panel for every site you create—similar to a car’s dashboard that shows speed, fuel, and engine warnings, but for your online projects.

### 2.2 Key Sections at a Glance  

When you first log in, you’ll see a clean, tile‑based layout. The main sections you’ll interact with most often are:

- **My Sites** – A list of all sites you own. Each tile shows a thumbnail, status (Published/Draft), and quick actions (Edit, Preview, Delete).  
- **Site Actions** – Buttons that appear when you open a site’s menu: **Edit Site**, **View Site**, **Publish**, **Duplicate**, **Delete**.  
- **Settings** – Central place for domain connections, SEO basics, backups, and site permissions.  
- **Marketing & SEO** – Tools for email campaigns, social media posts, and basic search‑engine optimization.  
- **Apps** – Marketplace where you can add extra functionality (e.g., contact forms, chat widgets, booking systems).  
- **Analytics** – Overview of visitor statistics, traffic sources, and performance metrics (available on paid plans).  
- **Billing & Plans** – Manage subscription details, payment methods, and invoices.  

### 2.3 Walking Through the Dashboard  

1. **Locate “My Sites.”**  
   - This is the first tile on the home screen. Click any site thumbnail to open its **Site Dashboard**.  

2. **Open the Site Dashboard.**  
   - You’ll now see a vertical navigation bar on the left with the sections listed above. Clicking each label slides a new pane into view.  

3. **Explore “Settings.”**  
   - Inside Settings, you’ll find sub‑sections like **Domain**, **SEO (Google)**, **Business Info**, and **Backup & Restore**. These are where you’ll later configure your custom domain and SEO meta tags.  

4. **Check “Marketing & SEO.”**  
   - The first card usually offers a **“Site Booster”** suggestion (a paid SEO tool). You can ignore it for now, but note it’s where Wix nudges you toward premium features.  

5. **Visit “Apps.”**  
   - The App Market opens in a new tab. Browse categories such as “Blog,” “Online Store,” or “Social.” Adding an app will automatically create a new page or widget in your site.  

6. **Use “Analytics.”**  
   - On free plans, analytics are limited to basic visitor counts. On paid plans, you’ll see charts for **Page Views**, **Unique Visitors**, **Bounce Rate**, and more.  

> **Pro tip:** Keep the **Site Actions** button visible at all times. It provides a one‑click route back to the editor, preview mode, or publishing workflow—essential when you’re iterating quickly.

### 2.4 Customizing Your Dashboard View  

- **Drag‑and‑drop tiles** in “My Sites” to reorder them based on priority.  
- **Star favorite sites** by clicking the star icon on a site tile; starred sites appear at the top of the list.  
- **Toggle “Dark Mode”** (if available) via the profile menu for a more comfortable night‑time editing experience.

---

## 3. Wix ADI vs. Wix Editor: Which Tool Is Right for You?  

### 3.1 Defining the Two Builders  

- **Wix ADI (Artificial Design Intelligence)** – An automated site‑creation wizard. You answer a few simple questions (type of business, desired features, style preferences) and Wix generates a ready‑made site with pre‑filled content and layout.  

- **Wix Editor** – A manual, drag‑and‑drop interface that gives you full control over every element on the page. You start from a blank canvas or a template and arrange text boxes, images, strips, and widgets yourself.  

Both tools ultimately produce a Wix site, but the workflow and level of customization differ dramatically.

### 3.2 When to Choose Wix ADI  

| Situation | Why ADI Fits |
|-----------|--------------|
| **You need a site fast** – e.g., a last‑minute event page | ADI builds a complete site in minutes after a short questionnaire. |
| **You’re not comfortable with design tools** | The AI selects fonts, colors, and layout based on your answers, eliminating guesswork. |
| **Your site is simple** – a personal bio, single‑service landing page, or a basic portfolio | ADI provides clean, mobile‑responsive pages without extra steps. |
| **You prefer a guided experience** | ADI walks you through each decision, offering suggestions along the way. |

### 3.3 When to Choose Wix Editor  

| Situation | Why Editor Fits |
|-----------|-----------------|
| **You want granular design control** – precise placement, animations, custom shapes | The Editor lets you move every element pixel by pixel and add advanced interactions. |
| **You plan to use many Wix Apps** | Some apps integrate more seamlessly when added manually through the Editor. |
| **You need multiple page types** – blog, shop, events, members area | The Editor provides a full suite of page templates and layout options. |
| **You have brand guidelines** (specific colors, fonts, logo placement) | You can lock down styles and ensure consistency across the entire site. |
| **You enjoy learning design tools** | Working in the Editor builds skills that transfer to other platforms (e.g., Photoshop, Figma). |

### 3.4 Direct Comparison  

| Feature | Wix ADI | Wix Editor |
|---------|---------|------------|
| **Initial setup time** | 5‑10 minutes | 30 minutes + (depends on complexity) |
| **Design flexibility** | Limited to AI‑chosen layout | Unlimited (subject to Wix’s element library) |
| **Learning curve** | Very low – mostly answering prompts | Moderate – requires familiarity with drag‑and‑drop and layer management |
| **Customization after creation** | You can edit content but major layout changes may be restricted | Full edit of every element, section, and page structure |
| **Mobile responsiveness** | Automatic, but less tweakable | Automatic with the ability to fine‑tune mobile view separately |
| **Ideal user** | Beginners, time‑pressed creators, simple sites | Designers, marketers, businesses needing advanced features |

### 3.5 Decision Checklist  

- **Do you need a site in under an hour?** → **Yes → ADI**  
- **Do you have a brand style guide you must follow?** → **Yes → Editor**  
- **Will you be adding many third‑party apps later?** → **Yes → Editor**  
- **Do you feel comfortable learning a visual editor?** → **Yes → Editor**  
- **Otherwise, start with ADI and switch later** – Wix lets you convert an ADI site to the Editor at any time (though some AI‑generated elements may need manual adjustment).

### 3.6 Switching Between the Two  

If you begin with ADI and later decide you need more control:

1. Open the site’s **Dashboard**.  
2. Click **“Edit Site”**; you’ll be prompted with an option to **“Switch to Editor.”**  
3. Confirm the switch. Wix will recreate the current pages in the Editor, preserving content while unlocking full design tools.  

Conversely, you can always start with the Editor and later use the **“Wix ADI”** button (found under **Settings → Site Design**) to let the AI suggest a fresh redesign—though this is less common.

---

## 4. Quick Hands‑On: Build Your First Simple Page  

To cement the concepts, follow these three minutes of action:

1. **Log into the Dashboard** and click **“Create New Site.”**  
2. **Select “Start from Scratch”** (this opens the Editor) or **“Answer a Few Questions”** (ADI). Choose the option you feel most comfortable with.  
3. **If using ADI:**  
   - Answer the questionnaire (e.g., “I’m a photographer,” “I need a contact form”).  
   - Review the generated site, click **“Edit”**, change the placeholder text to your name, and upload a photo.  
4. **If using the Editor:**  
   - Drag a **“Strip”** onto the canvas, add a **“Text”** element, type “Welcome to My Portfolio,” and style it with the toolbar.  
   - Add an **“Image”** widget from the left panel, upload a picture, and align it beside the text.  

5. **Save** (top‑right button) and **Preview** to see how it looks on desktop and mobile.  

You now have a live site skeleton—ready for the deeper design work covered in later chapters.

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Creating an account** is the first concrete step; you’ll need a valid email and a password, and you can start on the free plan before upgrading.  
- **Subscription plans** differ in storage, branding removal, and e‑commerce capability—pick the tier that matches your current needs and budget.  
- **The Wix Dashboard** centralizes all site management tasks; the most frequently used sections are **My Sites, Settings, Marketing & SEO, Apps,** and **Analytics.**  
- **Wix ADI** offers a fast, guided way to launch simple sites, while **Wix Editor** provides granular design freedom for more complex projects.  
- You can start with ADI and later switch to the Editor (or vice‑versa) without losing your content, giving you flexibility as your confidence grows.  

With your account set up, your dashboard familiar, and a clear sense of which builder aligns with your goals, you’re ready to move on to selecting a template and shaping the visual identity of your Wix website.

modules.title: Choosing and Setting Up a Template
modules.content:
## A Real‑World Kick‑Start: Maya’s Pop‑Up Bakery  

Maya wants to launch a simple website for her pop‑up bakery in three days. She has already **created a Wix account** and logged in at **www.wix.com**, but she isn’t sure where to begin. Her goal is clear: choose a design that feels fresh, showcase her menu, and make the site look professional without spending hours on layout decisions. The fastest way to achieve this is to start with a **template** that matches her business type, then tweak the basic settings—site title, favicon, and language—so the site feels uniquely hers.

The steps below walk you through exactly what Maya (and you) need to do, from browsing the template gallery to publishing a polished, ready‑to‑go site.

---

## Browsing the Template Gallery  

When you’re ready to create a new site, the **Wix Dashboard** is your launch pad. From the Dashboard click **My Sites** → **Create New Site**. Wix will greet you with the **Template Gallery**, a collection of pre‑designed layouts organized by industry, purpose, and visual style.

### 1. Choose a Category that Matches Your Purpose  

1. **Select a purpose** – Wix asks, “What do you want to create?” Choose the option that best reflects your goal (e.g., **Business**, **Online Store**, **Portfolio**, **Blog**).  
2. **Pick a category** – After selecting a purpose, a list of categories appears (e.g., *Restaurant & Food*, *Health & Wellness*, *Photography*). For Maya, the **Restaurant & Food → Bakery** sub‑category is the logical pick.  

> **Tip:** Even if you don’t see an exact match, choose the nearest category. You can always replace images and text later.

### 2. Filter by Features, Layout, and Color  

Below the category tiles, you’ll find filter icons:

| Filter | What It Does |
|--------|--------------|
| **Style** | Shows templates with a particular aesthetic (minimalist, vibrant, classic). |
| **Layout** | Toggles between *single‑page* or *multi‑page* designs. |
| **Color** | Highlights templates that predominantly use a chosen color palette. |
| **Industry Tags** | Adds tags like *Coffee Shop*, *Dessert*, *Organic* to narrow results. |

Apply any combination that aligns with your brand identity. For a bakery that wants a warm, inviting feel, Maya might select **Style → Warm**, **Color → Earth Tones**, and the **Industry Tag → Bakery**.

### 3. Use the Search Bar for Keywords  

If you have a specific visual in mind, type keywords such as “rustic”, “modern”, or “minimalist” into the search bar. The gallery will surface templates whose metadata contains those words.

### 4. Preview Thumbnails Before You Commit  

Hovering over a thumbnail reveals a **quick preview** button. Clicking it opens a **full‑screen preview** where you can navigate through the home page, about page, and contact page (if present). This gives you a realistic sense of the template’s layout, typography, and image placeholders.

> **Pro Tip:** Open several previews in separate browser tabs. This makes side‑by‑side comparison painless when you later decide which template feels most “you”.

---

## Applying a Template to a New Site  

Once you’ve identified the perfect template, the next step is to **apply it** and start shaping your site.

### 1. Select the Template  

In the preview window, click the **“Edit”** button (or **“Choose This Template”** at the bottom). Wix will automatically create a new site using that template and take you straight to the **Wix Editor** (the visual canvas you met in *Getting Started with Wix*).

### 2. Immediate Preview of the Live Site  

Before you dive into editing, click the **Preview** icon (the eye‑shaped button) in the top‑right corner of the Editor. This toggles **Preview Mode**, showing exactly how visitors will see the site—no editing tools, just the rendered page. Use this view to verify that navigation works, images load correctly, and the overall flow feels natural.

### 3. Switching Templates (If Needed)  

If after a few minutes you feel the template isn’t a perfect fit, you can **change it without losing content**:

1. In the Editor, click **Site** → **Site Themes** → **Change Template**.  
2. Choose a new template from the gallery; Wix will ask whether to keep your existing content or start fresh.  
3. Confirm the choice, and Wix will re‑apply the new design while preserving the text you’ve entered.

> **Caution:** Switching templates after extensive customization may require re‑positioning elements, so it’s best to finalize the template early.

---

## Configuring Basic Site Settings  

Beyond the visual design, three core settings give your site its identity: **site title**, **favicon**, and **language**. These are managed from the **Wix Dashboard**, not the Editor.

### 1. Locate Site Settings  

1. From any page in the Editor, click the **Dashboard** icon (top‑left).  
2. In the Dashboard’s left‑hand menu, select **Settings**.  
3. Under **General**, you’ll see fields for **Site Title**, **Favicon**, and **Language**.

### 2. Set the Site Title  

The site title appears in browser tabs, search engine results, and as a default heading in many Wix templates.

- **Best practice:** Keep it under 60 characters, include your brand name, and optionally a keyword (e.g., “Maya’s Sweet Treats – Artisanal Bakery”).  
- **How to edit:** Click the **Site Title** field, type your new title, and press **Enter** or click **Save**.

### 3. Upload a Favicon  

A **favicon** (short for “favorite icon”) is the tiny 16 × 16‑pixel image that shows next to your site’s name in browser tabs and bookmarks.

1. Click the **Favicon** placeholder.  
2. Choose **Upload Image** and select a square PNG or ICO file (recommended size: **256 × 256 px**; Wix will resize it).  
3. After uploading, click **Apply**.  

> **Tip:** Use a simplified version of your logo—high contrast works best at tiny sizes.

### 4. Choose the Site Language  

The language setting determines the default text for Wix UI elements (e.g., button labels) and can affect SEO.

- Click the **Language** dropdown.  
- Select your primary language (e.g., **English (United States)**).  
- If you plan to serve multilingual audiences later, note that Wix offers a **Multilingual** app, but the basic language setting should match your main content.

### 5. Save and Publish  

After adjusting these settings, click **Save** at the top of the Settings panel. To make the site live, return to the **Wix Editor** and click **Publish**. Even if you’re not ready for the world, publishing now lets you share a **preview link** with collaborators for feedback.

---

## Step‑by‑Step Walkthrough: Maya’s Bakery Site  

Below is a concrete, end‑to‑end walk‑through that mirrors Maya’s experience. Follow each numbered step, and you’ll have a fully‑branded template ready for content insertion.

1. **Log In & Open Dashboard** – Visit **www.wix.com**, sign in, and click **My Sites**.  
2. **Create New Site** – Click the **“+ Create New Site”** button.  
3. **Select Purpose** – Choose **Business** → **Restaurant & Food** → **Bakery**.  
4. **Filter & Search** – Apply the **Style → Warm** filter and type “rustic” in the search bar.  
5. **Preview Templates** – Open three promising templates in separate tabs.  
6. **Pick the Best Fit** – Maya selects “Rustic Bakery” because its hero image matches her brand palette.  
7. **Apply Template** – Click **Edit**; Wix loads the **Wix Editor** with the chosen template.  
8. **Enter Preview Mode** – Click the **eye icon** to see the site as visitors will.  
9. **Open Settings** – From the Editor, click the **Dashboard** icon → **Settings**.  
10. **Edit Site Title** – Enter **“Maya’s Sweet Treats – Artisan Bakery”** and save.  
11. **Upload Favicon** – Choose a 256 × 256 px PNG of Maya’s logo monogram, apply it.  
12. **Set Language** – Select **English (United States)** from the dropdown.  
13. **Save Settings** – Click **Save** at the top of the Settings panel.  
14. **Publish** – Return to the Editor, click **Publish**, and copy the preview link to share with Maya’s friends for feedback.

At this point, Maya’s site has a professional look, a clear title, a recognizable favicon, and the correct language—ready for the next phase of adding her menu, photos, and contact form.

---

## Common Pitfalls & Pro Tips  

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | Quick Fix |
|---------|----------------|-----------|
| **Choosing a template that’s too complex** | Beginners get dazzled by flashy animations and many pages. | Start with a **single‑page** layout; you can add pages later. |
| **Forgot to upload a favicon** | Wix uses a default icon if none is provided, making the site look generic. | Upload a **square PNG** (256 × 256 px) before publishing. |
| **Site title exceeds 60 characters** | Search engines truncate long titles, reducing brand visibility. | Keep the title concise; place extra details in the **meta description** later. |
| **Selecting the wrong language** | The UI language may default to a language you don’t speak, causing confusion. | Double‑check the **Language** dropdown immediately after creating the site. |
| **Not saving after each change** | Wix autosaves, but settings changes in the Dashboard require an explicit **Save**. | After editing Site Title, Favicon, or Language, click **Save** before leaving the page. |

### Pro Tips for a Faster Setup  

- **Batch upload images**: If you have a logo set and a favicon ready, upload both in one go to avoid repeated file‑picker dialogs.  
- **Use the “Duplicate” feature**: If you create a test site to experiment, you can duplicate it (Dashboard → Site Actions → Duplicate) and keep the original as a clean backup.  
- **Leverage the “Undo” shortcut** (Ctrl + Z / Cmd + Z) while editing, especially when moving elements that may affect layout.

---

## Why the Right Template Matters  

Choosing a template isn’t just about aesthetics; it influences **site structure**, **navigation flow**, and **future scalability**. A bakery template typically includes:

- A **hero section** for a featured product or promotion.  
- A **menu or product grid** that can be repurposed for daily specials.  
- A **contact form** for catering inquiries.  

By starting with a template that already contains these sections, you save time and reduce the need for extensive custom coding or third‑party apps later on.

---

## Next Steps  

Now that you have a template installed and the core site settings configured, you’re ready to dive into the **Wix Editor Interface** (next chapter). There you’ll learn how to edit text, replace images, and rearrange sections to truly make the site yours.

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Browse the Template Gallery** by purpose, category, and filters; use the search bar and preview thumbnails to narrow choices.  
- **Apply a template** through the “Edit” button, then use **Preview Mode** to see the live look before editing.  
- **Configure basic settings** (site title, favicon, language) from the **Wix Dashboard → Settings**; these settings affect SEO, branding, and user experience.  
- Follow a **step‑by‑step workflow** (create site → select template → preview → edit settings → publish) to avoid missing essential configurations.  
- Avoid common pitfalls such as oversized titles, missing favicons, or unsaved changes, and apply pro tips like batch uploading and using the duplicate feature for experimentation.  

With a suitable template in place and the foundational settings tuned, your Wix site is primed for the next phase: adding and customizing content that tells your story.

modules.content:
## A Real‑World Moment: Turning a Blank Page into a Landing‑Page Prototype  

Imagine you’ve just selected a sleek “Tech Startup” template in the Wix Dashboard. The site loads, and the canvas is populated with placeholder text, images, and a navigation bar. You’re eager to replace the generic hero image with a photo of your own product, move the call‑to‑action button to a more prominent spot, and tweak the color of the heading. Yet, staring at the screen, you’re not sure which part of the interface lets you do each of those tasks.  

This chapter walks you through the exact tools, panels, and shortcuts you’ll need to reshape any template—no prior design experience required. By the end, you’ll be able to locate the **Toolbar**, **Add Panel**, and **Settings Menu**, move elements confidently with drag‑and‑drop, and employ undo/redo and copy/paste shortcuts to work faster and safer.

---

## 1. The Wix Editor Canvas – Where Your Site Lives  

The central area of the Wix Editor is called the **canvas**. It is the visual representation of the page you are editing; everything you see here will appear to visitors once the site is published. Think of the canvas as a digital drafting table: you place, arrange, and style elements directly on it.

### 1.1. The Toolbar – Your Command Center  

Running horizontally across the top of the editor, the Toolbar houses the most frequently used actions. Each icon is a button that opens a submenu or activates a mode. The core groups you’ll interact with in this chapter are:

| Icon | Name (first appearance) | Primary Use |
|------|------------------------|-------------|
| ![Select icon] | **Select** | Click to activate the cursor for selecting, moving, or resizing elements. |
| ![Add icon] | **Add** (opens the Add Panel) | Insert new elements—text, images, buttons, strips, etc. |
| ![Design icon] | **Design** | Adjust visual styles such as colors, borders, and shadows. |
| ![Settings icon] | **Settings** | Open the Settings Menu for the selected element or the whole site. |
| ![Preview icon] | **Preview** | See how the page looks to visitors without leaving the editor. |
| ![Publish icon] | **Publish** | Make your changes live (covered in later chapters). |

> **Tip:** Hover over an icon to see a tooltip that names the tool; this is especially helpful when you’re still learning the icons.

#### 1.1.1. Selecting the Right Tool  

- **Select** – Use this as the default mode. When an element is highlighted with a blue outline, you can drag it, resize its handles, or open its settings.  
- **Add** – Click once to open the Add Panel (covered next).  
- **Design** – Appears only after you have an element selected; it provides quick access to style options specific to that element.  

---

## 2. The Add Panel – Your Library of Building Blocks  

When you click the **Add** icon, a vertical panel slides out from the left side of the screen. This is the **Add Panel**, the hub for every content element you can place on your site.

### 2.1. Navigating the Add Panel  

The panel is organized into intuitive categories:

1. **Text** – Headings, paragraphs, quotes, and lists.  
2. **Images & Media** – Photos, galleries, video players, and audio tracks.  
3. **Buttons & Menus** – Call‑to‑action buttons, navigation menus, social icons.  
4. **Strip & Columns** – Full‑width strips, column layouts, and grids.  
5. **More** – Widgets such as calendars, contact forms, and social feeds.  

At the top of the panel is a **search bar**. Typing “map” instantly filters the list to show only map‑related widgets, saving you time when you know exactly what you need.

### 2.2. Adding an Element: Step‑by‑Step  

1. **Open the Add Panel** – Click the **Add** icon on the Toolbar.  
2. **Choose a Category** – For example, click **Images & Media**.  
3. **Select an Element** – Hover over “Image” and click the **+ Add** button that appears.  
4. **Place on Canvas** – The image drops onto the canvas where your cursor is positioned.  
5. **Adjust Position** – Drag the newly added element to its final spot (see Section 3).  

> **Pro tip:** After adding an element, the **Design** and **Settings** icons on the Toolbar become active, letting you style or configure the element without leaving the canvas.

---

## 3. The Settings Menu – Fine‑Tuning Your Elements  

Every element you place on the canvas has a set of properties that control its behavior, layout, and advanced options. Access to these properties is provided by the **Settings Menu**, which appears on the right side of the editor when an element is selected.

### 3.1. What the Settings Menu Looks Like  

The Settings Menu is a vertical pane divided into tabs. The exact tabs depend on the element type, but common sections include:

- **Layout** – Alignment, margins, padding, and positioning (absolute vs. fixed).  
- **Design** – Colors, borders, shadows, and animation effects.  
- **Text** – Font family, size, line height, and letter spacing (for text elements).  
- **SEO** – Alt text for images, link titles, and other search‑engine‑friendly attributes.  
- **Advanced** – Custom CSS, ID tags, and data attributes (available for more experienced users).  

### 3.2. Quick Settings You’ll Use Frequently  

| Setting | Where to Find | Typical Use |
|---------|----------------|-------------|
| **Resize** | Canvas handles (drag corners) | Make an image larger or smaller. |
| **Position** | **Layout** tab | Align a button to the center of its container. |
| **Link** | **Design** tab → **Link** | Turn a text block into a hyperlink. |
| **Animation** | **Design** tab → **Animation** | Add a fade‑in effect when the page loads. |
| **Alt Text** | **SEO** tab | Describe an image for screen readers and search engines. |

> **Remember:** Any change you make in the Settings Menu can be undone with the shortcut described in Section 4, so feel free to experiment.

---

## 4. Working With Elements – Drag‑and‑Drop Mastery  

Once an element is on the canvas, you’ll spend most of your time moving it, resizing it, and aligning it with other elements. Wix’s drag‑and‑drop system is designed to be intuitive, but a few built‑in aids make precision easier.

### 4.1. Basic Drag‑and‑Drop  

1. **Select** the element by clicking anywhere on it.  
2. **Grab** the element (the cursor changes to a hand) and **drag** it to the desired location.  
3. **Release** the mouse button to drop the element.  

While dragging, Wix shows **smart guides**—thin gray lines that appear when the element is aligned with the center or edges of other objects. These guides help you achieve a balanced layout without measuring manually.

### 4.2. Resizing With Handles  

When an element is selected, small squares appear at its corners and mid‑sides. Drag a corner handle to scale proportionally, or drag a side handle to adjust width or height independently. Holding **Shift** while dragging a corner maintains the original aspect ratio.

### 4.3. Aligning Multiple Elements  

- **Select Multiple Elements** – Hold **Ctrl** (Windows) or **⌘ Command** (Mac) and click each element you want to group.  
- **Align Buttons** – Once multiple elements are selected, the **Design** icon on the Toolbar expands to show alignment options: Align Left, Center, Right, Top, Middle, Bottom. Click the desired alignment to snap all selected items together.  

### 4.4. Using the Keyboard for Precision  

- **Nudge** – Arrow keys move the selected element 1 px at a time. Holding **Shift** while pressing an arrow key nudges 10 px.  
- **Duplicate** – Press **Ctrl + D** (Windows) or **⌘ + D** (Mac) to create an exact copy of the selected element, which appears directly on top. Drag the duplicate to its new spot.  

---

## 5. Keyboard Shortcuts – Speeding Up Your Workflow  

Memorizing a handful of shortcuts can dramatically reduce the time you spend clicking through menus. Below are the shortcuts most useful for beginners, listed for both Windows and macOS. All shortcuts work when the Wix Editor is active (i.e., the canvas or any panel is focused).

| Action | Windows Shortcut | macOS Shortcut |
|--------|------------------|----------------|
| **Undo** | **Ctrl + Z** | **⌘ + Z** |
| **Redo** | **Ctrl + Y** or **Ctrl + Shift + Z** | **⌘ + Shift + Z** |
| **Copy** | **Ctrl + C** | **⌘ + C** |
| **Paste** | **Ctrl + V** | **⌘ + V** |
| **Duplicate** | **Ctrl + D** | **⌘ + D** |
| **Select All** | **Ctrl + A** | **⌘ + A** |
| **Delete** | **Delete** or **Backspace** | **Delete** or **Backspace** |
| **Nudge (1 px)** | **Arrow keys** | **Arrow keys** |
| **Nudge (10 px)** | **Shift + Arrow** | **Shift + Arrow** |
| **Open Settings** | **F2** (when element selected) | **F2** |

### 5.1. Practicing Undo/Redo  

A common fear for beginners is “breaking” a design. The **Undo** shortcut (**Ctrl + Z / ⌘ + Z**) instantly restores the previous state, while **Redo** lets you move forward again if you change your mind. Because Wix records every action, you can press Undo repeatedly to backtrack several steps.

### 5.2. Efficient Copy/Paste  

When you need the same element in multiple places (e.g., a button that appears on three sections), copy it (**Ctrl + C / ⌘ + C**) and paste (**Ctrl + V / ⌘ + V**). The pasted element retains all styling, so you only have to reposition it.

### 5.3. Shortcut Cheat Sheet  

Print the table above or keep it open in a separate browser tab while you work. Over time, the muscle memory will develop, and you’ll find yourself reaching for the keyboard before the mouse.

---

## 6. Putting It All Together – A Mini‑Project  

To cement the concepts, let’s walk through a realistic scenario: **Creating a custom hero section** for the “Tech Startup” template you opened earlier.

### 6.1. Goal  

- Replace the placeholder hero image with a product screenshot.  
- Add a headline, sub‑headline, and a “Request Demo” button.  
- Align everything centrally and apply a fade‑in animation.

### 6.2. Step‑by‑Step Walkthrough  

| Step | Action | Shortcut / Tool |
|------|--------|-----------------|
| **1** | **Select** the existing hero image on the canvas. | Click → **Select** icon (default). |
| **2** | **Delete** the placeholder image. | **Delete** key. |
| **3** | Open the **Add Panel** and insert a new **Image**. | Click **Add** → **Images & Media** → **Image** → **+ Add**. |
| **4** | Choose your product screenshot from the file manager and place it. | Click the file, then click anywhere on the canvas. |
| **5** | **Resize** the image to cover the full width of the strip. | Drag side handles while holding **Shift** for proportional scaling. |
| **6** | **Add** a **Text** element for the headline. | **Add** → **Text** → **Title** → **+ Add**. |
| **7** | Type “Introducing the Next‑Gen Dashboard”. | Click inside the text box and type. |
| **8** | **Style** the headline: change font to “Montserrat”, size to 48 px, color to #ffffff. | With the headline selected, click **Design** → **Edit Text**, then adjust settings. |
| **9** | **Duplicate** the headline to create a sub‑headline, then edit the text. | **Ctrl + D / ⌘ + D**, then edit. |
| **10** | **Add** a **Button** for “Request Demo”. | **Add** → **Button** → **+ Add**. |
| **11** | **Link** the button to a contact form page. | Select button → **Settings** → **Link** → choose the page. |
| **12** | **Align** the three elements (headline, sub‑headline, button) centrally. | Hold **Ctrl / ⌘** and click each element, then click **Design** → **Align Center**. |
| **13** | Apply a **Fade‑In** animation to the whole strip. | Select the strip (background area) → **Design** → **Animation** → choose “Fade In”. |
| **14** | **Preview** the page to confirm layout. | Click **Preview** icon on the Toolbar. |
| **15** | **Undo** any unwanted change, then **Save**. | **Ctrl + Z / ⌘ + Z** for Undo, then click **Save** (or **Ctrl + S**). |

During steps 6‑11, notice how the **Design** and **Settings** icons become active as soon as an element is selected—this is the seamless integration between the Toolbar and Settings Menu we highlighted earlier.

### 6.3. Reflection  

- **Drag‑and‑drop** let you position the image and button quickly.  
- **Smart guides** ensured the headline stayed centered without manual measurement.  
- **Undo/Redo** gave you confidence to experiment with font sizes and colors.  
- **Copy/Paste** (via duplicate) saved time when creating the sub‑headline.  

If you follow this workflow on any template, you’ll be able to replace placeholder content with your own branding in minutes.

---

## 7. Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them  

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | Quick Fix |
|---------|----------------|-----------|
| **Accidentally moving an element off‑canvas** | Dragging too far without noticing the canvas edges. | Use the **Zoom** slider (bottom‑right) to see the full page, or press **Ctrl + 0** (Windows) / **⌘ + 0** (Mac) to reset zoom. |
| **Forgetting to save after many changes** | Relying solely on auto‑save can lead to data loss if the browser crashes. | Press **Ctrl + S / ⌘ + S** after a batch of edits. |
| **Overusing copy/paste and creating duplicate IDs** | Copying elements that have unique IDs (used for linking) can cause conflicts. | After pasting, open the **Settings → Advanced** tab and verify the ID is unique, or let Wix generate a new one automatically. |
| **Ignoring the smart guides** | Manually aligning elements can lead to uneven spacing. | Keep an eye on the gray alignment lines; they appear automatically as you move items. |
| **Not using undo after a mistake** | Feeling stuck after a change. | Remember that **Undo** works for almost every action, even after switching panels. |

---

## 8. Next Steps  

Now that you’re comfortable navigating the Toolbar, Add Panel, and Settings Menu, the next logical step is to explore **Building Pages and Managing Site Structure** (Chapter 4). You’ll learn how to add new pages, reorder them, and set up navigation menus—building on the element‑placement skills you’ve just mastered.

---

## Key Takeaways  

- The **Toolbar** at the top provides quick access to selection, adding, designing, and settings tools.  
- The **Add Panel** on the left is your library of elements; use categories or the search bar to locate items quickly.  
- The **Settings Menu** on the right lets you fine‑tune layout, design, SEO, and advanced options for any selected element.  
- **Drag‑and‑drop** is the primary method for positioning elements; smart guides help you align items precisely.  
- Mastering a handful of **keyboard shortcuts**—undo/redo (**Ctrl/⌘ + Z**, **Shift + ⌘ + Z**), copy/paste (**Ctrl/⌘ + C/V**), duplicate (**Ctrl/⌘ + D**)—significantly speeds up editing and reduces errors.  
- Practice by recreating a hero section: replace placeholder content, add text and buttons, align centrally, and apply an animation—all within a few minutes using the tools and shortcuts described.  

With these fundamentals, you’re ready to transform any Wix template into a site that reflects your vision—one element at a time.

modules.title: Building Pages and Managing Site Structure
modules.content:
## Why a Clear Site Structure Matters  

Imagine you are opening a **virtual storefront** for a boutique coffee shop. A visitor lands on the homepage, sees a tempting photo of a latte, and wants to learn more about the shop’s story, the full drink menu, and how to place an online order. If the site’s pages are scattered, the menu is tangled, and links are missing, the visitor will quickly become frustrated and leave.  

A well‑organized page hierarchy and intuitive navigation do three things for beginners like you:

* **Guide visitors** to the information they need in as few clicks as possible.  
* **Signal professionalism** to both users and search engines.  
* **Make future updates** (adding a new “Seasonal Specials” page, for example) painless.

The steps below walk you through creating, arranging, and linking pages in Wix so that every visitor can find their way—no matter how many pages you eventually add.

---

## Adding New Pages  

### 1. Open the Wix Editor  

From the **Wix Dashboard** → **My Sites**, click **Select Site** and then **Edit Site**. The editor you explored in *Understanding the Wix Editor Interface* will appear.

### 2. Locate the Pages Panel  

On the left‑hand side, click the **Pages** icon (it looks like a stack of sheets). This panel lists every page currently in your site.

### 3. Create a Blank Page  

1. Click **+ Add Page** at the bottom of the panel.  
2. In the dialog, type a descriptive name (e.g., **Menu**, **About Us**, **Contact**).  
3. Choose **Blank Page** if you want to start from scratch, or pick a **Pre‑Designed Layout** (covered next).  
4. Click **Done**. The new page appears in the panel and opens on the canvas.

> **Tip:** Keep page names short and intuitive; these names become the default menu labels unless you edit them later.

### 4. Duplicate an Existing Page (Optional)  

If you need a page with a similar layout (say, multiple “Event” pages), hover over an existing page in the panel, click the three‑dot menu, and select **Duplicate**. Rename the copy to fit its purpose.

---

## Choosing a Page Layout  

Wix offers **page layouts**—pre‑arranged structures of sections, columns, and placeholders—that speed up design.

### 1. Access Layout Options  

When you add a new page, the **Add Page** dialog includes a **Layouts** tab. Click it to browse categories such as **Business**, **Portfolio**, **Blog**, and **Online Store**.

### 2. Pick a Layout That Matches the Page Goal  

| Layout Type | Ideal Use | Typical Sections |
|-------------|-----------|------------------|
| **Blank** | Full creative control | None (start from zero) |
| **Header + Text + Image** | About or service pages | Hero header, intro text, image |
| **Gallery** | Portfolio or product showcase | Image grid, lightbox |
| **Contact** | Contact page | Form, map, social icons |

Select the layout that best reflects the content you plan to add. Wix will automatically insert the corresponding sections onto the canvas.

### 3. Customize the Layout  

Even after choosing a layout, you can **add**, **move**, or **delete** sections:

* Click the **+ Add** button (top left) to insert new strips, columns, or widgets.  
* Hover over a section’s edge to drag it up or down.  
* Click the trash‑can icon on a section to remove it.

Remember, the layout is just a **starting point**—you’ll refine it later when adding content elements (next chapter).

---

## Organizing Your Navigation  

A clean navigation menu mirrors the logical flow of your site’s information. Wix lets you arrange pages hierarchically and control how they appear in the menu.

### 1. Open the Menu Settings  

In the **Pages** panel, click the **Menu & Pages** button at the top (it looks like a small list). This opens the **Site Menu** view, showing the current order of pages as they appear in the top navigation bar.

### 2. Reorder Pages  

* Drag a page up or down to change its position.  
* The order you set here is the order visitors see from left to right (or top to bottom on mobile).

### 3. Create Submenus (Dropdowns)  

1. Hover over the page that will become the **parent** (e.g., **Shop**).  
2. Click the three‑dot menu and select **Add Subpage**.  
3. Name the subpage (e.g., **Coffee**, **Tea**, **Merchandise**).  
4. The new page automatically nests under the parent, forming a dropdown when the site is previewed.

> **Note:** Subpages can themselves have sub‑subpages, but keep nesting to **two levels** for usability. Deep hierarchies confuse visitors and can hurt SEO.

### 4. Hide Pages from the Menu  

If you need a page that should be reachable only via a button or link (like a **Thank You** page after a form submission):

1. In the **Pages** panel, click the three‑dot menu for that page.  
2. Toggle **Show in Menu** off.  
The page remains part of your site and can be linked elsewhere, but it won’t appear in the main navigation.

### 5. Rename Menu Labels (Optional)  

Sometimes a page name isn’t ideal for a menu label. To edit:

1. Click the page name in the **Menu & Pages** view.  
2. Type the new label (e.g., change **Contact_Us** to **Contact**).  
3. Press **Enter** to save.

---

## Linking Pages  

Now that your pages exist and are organized, you need to **connect** them so visitors can move between them. Wix provides three primary linking methods: **buttons**, **text links**, and **menu items**.

### 1. Linking via Buttons  

1. In the Wix Editor, click **+ Add** → **Button** and drag a style onto the canvas.  
2. With the button selected, click the **Link** icon (chain link).  
3. In the **Link To** dialog, choose **Page** → **Site Pages**, then select the target page (e.g., **Menu**).  
4. Click **Done**.  
5. Optionally, change the button text (e.g., “View Full Menu”).

> **Pro tip:** Use **anchor links** for one‑page sites—link a button to a specific section on the same page. Choose **Anchor** in the Link dialog and pick the desired anchor.

### 2. Linking via Text  

1. Highlight the text you want to turn into a link (e.g., “Learn more about our story”).  
2. Click the **Link** icon that appears above the text.  
3. Choose **Page** → **Site Pages**, then pick the destination (e.g., **About Us**).  
4. Click **Done**.  

The linked text will automatically adopt an underline or color change, signaling interactivity.

### 3. Linking via the Menu  

If you’ve set up a hierarchical menu, the menu items already point to their respective pages. To adjust a menu link:

1. In **Menu & Pages**, click the page you want to edit.  
2. Use the **Link To** dropdown to switch between **Page**, **Anchor**, **External URL**, or **Document**.

### 4. Linking to External URLs  

Sometimes you need to point visitors outside of your Wix site (e.g., to an Instagram profile):

1. Open the **Link** dialog for a button or text.  
2. Select **Web Address** and paste the full URL (including https://).  
3. Toggle **Open in New Window** if you don’t want to replace the current page.  

### 5. Linking to Documents or Media  

If you have a downloadable PDF menu:

1. Click **+ Add** → **Document** → **Upload Document**.  
2. After uploading, the document appears as a button or icon.  
3. Click its **Link** settings, choose **Document**, and select the uploaded file.  

Visitors who click will download or view the PDF, depending on their browser settings.

---

## Testing Your Navigation  

Before publishing, always **preview** and **test** every link.

### 1. Use Preview Mode  

Click the **Preview** button (top right). The site loads in a live‑like view where you can:

* Click menu items, buttons, and text links.  
* Navigate through submenus to ensure dropdowns work.  
* Verify that hidden pages are reachable only via intended links.

### 2. Check Mobile Navigation  

While still in Preview, switch to **Mobile View** (icon looks like a smartphone). Mobile menus often collapse into a hamburger icon; ensure:

* All top‑level pages are listed.  
* Submenus appear as expandable sections.  
* Links still function after the menu expands.

### 3. Fix Broken Links  

If a link doesn’t work:

1. Return to the editor.  
2. Select the offending element.  
3. Open its **Link** settings and verify the correct page or URL is chosen.  

Wix also shows a **warning icon** next to any page that is orphaned (no incoming links). Consider adding at least one navigation path to such pages, or intentionally keep them hidden if they serve a special purpose.

---

## Managing Ongoing Changes  

Your site will evolve—new products, blog posts, or events may require additional pages.

* **Add pages** following the same steps; they automatically join the menu unless you hide them.  
* **Reorder** pages anytime by dragging them in the **Menu & Pages** view.  
* **Rename** pages or menu labels without affecting existing links; Wix updates the link targets automatically.  

Keeping the navigation tidy is an ongoing task, but the workflow remains consistent, making future edits quick and low‑stress.

---

## Common Beginner Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them  

| Pitfall | Why It Happens | Quick Fix |
|---------|----------------|-----------|
| **Too many top‑level items** | Adding every page directly to the main menu | Group related pages under a parent (e.g., **Shop** > **Coffee**, **Tea**) |
| **Orphan pages** (no links) | Forgetting to add a button or menu entry after creating a page | Use the **Pages** panel warning icon to locate orphans and add a link |
| **Broken links after renaming** | Changing a page name but not updating the link | Wix automatically updates internal links; double‑check external links or anchors |
| **Dropdowns not opening on mobile** | Submenus designed for desktop only | In **Mobile View**, ensure the “Hamburger” menu includes the subpages; test on a real device if possible |
| **Overly long URLs** (e.g., `www.yoursite.com/page123`) | Using default auto‑generated page names | Rename pages to concise, readable names before publishing (e.g., **Contact**) |

---

## Quick Reference Checklist  

- [ ] **Add all required pages** (Home, About, Services, Contact, etc.).  
- [ ] **Select an appropriate layout** for each page.  
- [ ] **Arrange pages** in a logical order in the **Menu & Pages** view.  
- [ ] **Create submenus** for related groups of pages.  
- [ ] **Link pages** using buttons, text links, and menu items.  
- [ ] **Test navigation** in both desktop and mobile preview modes.  
- [ ] **Fix any orphan or broken links** before publishing.

---

## Key Takeaways  

* **Pages are the building blocks** of your Wix site; add them via the Pages panel and pick a layout that matches the page’s purpose.  
* **A hierarchical menu** (parent → subpages) keeps navigation clean and guides visitors intuitively.  
* **Linking methods**—buttons, text links, and menu items—let you connect pages wherever it makes sense for the user experience.  
* **Always preview and test** on both desktop and mobile to ensure every link works and menus behave as expected.  
* **Maintain a tidy navigation** by regularly reviewing the menu order, hiding pages that should be accessed only via specific links, and avoiding deep nesting.  

With these fundamentals, you now have a solid framework for constructing a navigable, user‑friendly Wix website—ready for the next step of adding and customizing content.

modules.title: Adding and Customizing Content Elements
modules.content:
## A Real‑World Prompt: The Bakery That Wants to Wow Online Visitors  

Imagine you’ve just opened *Sweet Crumbs*, a cozy bakery on Main Street. You’ve already chosen a bright, food‑friendly template and laid out the basic pages (home, about, menu, contact) using the Wix Editor. Now it’s time to fill those pages with the things that will make customers stop scrolling: **delicious‑looking photos**, **mouth‑watering descriptions**, **a gallery of seasonal treats**, **a short video of frosting being piped**, and **a simple way for visitors to ask about catering**.  

All of those pieces are *content elements*—the building blocks that turn a blank page into a vibrant, functional experience. In the sections that follow you’ll learn, step by step, how to add and style each type of element, and how to bring in interactive widgets from the Wix App Market. By the end of this chapter you’ll be able to replicate the Sweet Crumbs example (or any other business) with confidence, even if you’ve never touched a website before.

---

## Adding Text: Boxes, Headings, and Typography  

### Inserting a Text Box  

1. **Select the Add (+) button** on the left‑hand toolbar of the Wix Editor.  
2. Hover over **Text** and click **Add Text**.  
3. A placeholder text box appears on the canvas. Drag it to the desired spot and resize it by dragging the handles.  

> **Tip:** If you need a pre‑styled block (e.g., a paragraph with a background color), choose one of the *Text Presets* that appear under the same menu.

### Using Headings for Structure  

Headings (H1, H2, H3, …) are the hierarchy that tells both readers and search engines how your content is organized.  

- **H1** – Use only once per page, typically for the main title (“Our Menu”).  
- **H2** – Sub‑sections (“Cakes”, “Pastries”).  
- **H3** – Further detail (“Chocolate Cake”, “Gluten‑Free Muffins”).  

To change a text box into a heading:  

1. Click the box to open the **Text Toolbar**.  
2. Click the **Paragraph** dropdown and select **Heading 2** (or whichever level you need).  

### Formatting Typography  

The **Design** panel gives you full control over font‑related styles.  

| Setting | What It Does | How to Access |
|---------|--------------|---------------|
| **Font Family** | Chooses the typeface (e.g., *Montserrat*). | Click the **Font** field in the Text Settings. |
| **Size** | Adjusts the visual height of the letters. | Use the **Size** slider or type a value (e.g., 24 px). |
| **Color** | Sets the text color. | Click the color swatch; you can enter a hex code or pick from the palette. |
| **Line Height** | Controls the vertical spacing between lines of text. | Adjust the **Line Height** slider (default is 1.4). |
| **Letter Spacing** | Adds or removes space between individual characters. | Use the **Letter Spacing** control. |

**Bold**, *italic*, and **underline** shortcuts appear in the Text Toolbar for quick emphasis.  

> **Pro tip:** For readability on mobile devices, avoid font sizes smaller than 14 px and keep line height around 1.5.

### Quick Tip: Text Toolbar vs. Settings Panel  

- **Text Toolbar** (appears when you click a text box) offers *instant* formatting—bold, align, list, link.  
- **Settings Panel** (opens on the right when you click **Edit Text**) provides deeper options such as **Typography**, **Spacing**, and **Advanced CSS** (if you’re comfortable with code).  

Use the Toolbar for rapid tweaks; switch to Settings when you need precise control.

---

## Working with Images: Upload, Edit, and Position  

### Uploading Images  

1. Click **Add (+)** → **Image** → **My Uploads**.  
2. In the **Media Manager**, click **Upload Media** and choose **From Computer** (or drag‑and‑drop).  
3. Once uploaded, the image appears in **My Uploads**; click it to place it on the page.  

You can also pull images directly from Wix’s free **Media Library**, which contains stock photos organized by category.

### Basic Image Editing  

When you select an image, a mini‑toolbar appears with icons for:

- **Crop** – Drag the handles to trim excess space.  
- **Rotate** – Click the rotate arrow to turn the image 90° increments.  
- **Filters** – Apply preset color overlays (e.g., *Sepia*, *Brighten*).  
- **Replace** – Swap the picture without losing positioning or size.  

All edits are non‑destructive; you can revert to the original at any time via the **Reset** button.

### Positioning and Alignment  

- **Drag** the image to the desired location.  
- Use the **Alignment Guides** (blue lines) that appear automatically to snap the image to the grid or other elements.  
- For precise placement, open the **Layout** tab in the Settings panel and set **Margins** (top, right, bottom, left) in pixels.  

### Adding Alt Text for Accessibility  

**Alt text** (alternative text) describes the image for screen readers and improves SEO.  

1. With the image selected, click **Settings** → **Accessibility**.  
2. Enter a concise description (e.g., “Chocolate cake with raspberry glaze”).  

Never leave alt text blank; even a brief phrase adds value.

---

## Building Image Galleries  

### Choosing a Gallery Layout  

The Wix Editor offers several gallery styles:

- **Grid** – Uniform rows and columns; great for product listings.  
- **Masonry** – Staggered, uneven heights; ideal for artistic portfolios.  
- **Slider** – Horizontal slide show; perfect for storytelling.  
- **Strip** – Full‑width panoramic display; works well for hero sections.  

Select a style by clicking **Add (+)** → **Gallery** and then choosing the layout that matches your design goal.

### Adding Images to a Gallery  

1. Drag the gallery placeholder onto the page.  
2. Click **Manage Media** → **Add Images**.  
3. Choose images from **My Uploads** or the **Wix Media Library**.  
4. Click **Apply**; the gallery updates automatically.  

### Customizing Gallery Settings  

In the **Gallery Settings** panel you can adjust:

- **Spacing** – Gap between thumbnails (default 10 px).  
- **Hover Effects** – Choose between *Zoom*, *Overlay*, or *None*.  
- **Transition** – For sliders, set the animation type (e.g., *Fade*, *Slide*).  
- **Lightbox** – Enable a pop‑up view when a visitor clicks an image; you can customize the background color and navigation arrows.  

### Responsive Gallery Tips  

- **Set Width to 100 %** in the Layout tab so the gallery stretches across the screen on larger devices.  
- **Preview** on the mobile view (top‑right of the editor) to ensure images don’t become too small; adjust **Columns** for mobile if needed.  

---

## Embedding Videos  

### Adding a Video Player from Wix  

1. Click **Add (+)** → **Video** → **Video Player**.  
2. Drag the player onto the canvas.  
3. In the **Video Settings**, click **Change Video** and paste a **YouTube** or **Vimeo** URL, or select a video you’ve uploaded to Wix.  

### Using YouTube/Vimeo Links  

Embedding a video via URL has several advantages:

- **No extra storage**—the video remains on the host platform.  
- **Automatic updates**—if you replace the video on YouTube, the embedded version updates instantly.  

Make sure the video’s **privacy settings** allow embedding (public or unlisted).

### Autoplay, Loop, and Controls  

Within the **Video Settings** you can toggle:

- **Autoplay** – Starts the video as soon as the page loads (use sparingly; it can be intrusive).  
- **Loop** – Replays the video continuously.  
- **Show Controls** – Displays the play/pause bar; turn off for a cleaner look if you provide a custom play button.  

### Styling Video Frames  

The same **Design** panel used for images applies to videos. You can:

- Add a **border radius** (e.g., 8 px) for rounded corners.  
- Apply a **shadow** to make the player stand out.  
- Choose a **background color** that matches your site’s palette.  

---

## Interactive Widgets: Wix Apps Basics  

### Accessing the Wix App Market  

The **Wix App Market** is a repository of third‑party and Wix‑built widgets that add functionality beyond the core editor.  

1. In the left toolbar, click **App Market** (shopping‑bag icon).  
2. Use the search bar or browse categories such as *Business Tools*, *Social*, or *Marketing*.  

All apps have a **Free** tier; premium features may require a paid plan.

### Adding a Contact Form  

A contact form lets visitors send messages without leaving your site.  

1. Search for **Wix Forms** in the App Market and click **Add to Site**.  
2. Choose a preset layout (e.g., *Simple Contact*).  
3. The form appears on the page; click it to open the **Form Settings**.  

**Key fields to configure:**  

- **Email Recipient** – Where form submissions are sent.  
- **Thank‑You Message** – Text displayed after submission.  
- **Field Labels** – Ensure each input (Name, Email, Message) is clearly labeled.  

You can also add a **reCAPTCHA** checkbox for spam protection via the **Advanced Settings** tab.

### Adding a Social Feed  

A social feed displays your latest Instagram, Facebook, or Twitter posts, keeping the site fresh.  

1. Search for **Instagram Feed** (or the platform you use).  
2. Click **Add to Site** and position the widget where you want it (e.g., below the gallery).  
3. Connect the feed by entering your **username** and authorizing Wix to access the account.  

**Customization options** include:

- **Number of posts** displayed.  
- **Layout** (grid vs. carousel).  
- **Hover overlay** (show likes/comments).  

### Adding a Map  

For a bakery, a map helps customers find your physical location.  

1. Search for **Wix Maps** and click **Add to Site**.  
2. Drag the map onto the page.  
3. In the **Map Settings**, type your address (e.g., “123 Main St, Springfield”).  
4. Adjust the **Zoom Level** and **Map Style** (standard, satellite, or hybrid).  

You can enable **Directions** so visitors can click a button to get turn‑by‑turn navigation.

### Configuring App Settings  

Every app added to your site appears in the **Site Structure** panel under **Apps**.  

- **Visibility** – Choose whether the widget shows on desktop, mobile, or both.  
- **Position** – Use the **Layers** menu to bring the widget forward or send it backward relative to other elements.  
- **Styling** – Most apps include a **Design** tab where you can adjust colors, fonts, and borders to match your site’s theme.  

---

## Styling and Layering Content Elements  

### Using the Design Panel  

When any element is selected, the right‑hand **Design** tab offers quick styling controls:

- **Background** – Solid color, gradient, or image.  
- **Border** – Width, style (solid, dashed), and color.  
- **Shadow** – Offset, blur, and opacity.  

These options let you keep a consistent visual language across text, images, and widgets.

### Arranging Order (Bring to Front, Send Back)  

Elements can overlap; the order matters.  

- Right‑click an element and choose **Arrange → Bring to Front** or **Send to Back**.  
- For finer control, select **Arrange → Move Forward/Backward One Layer**.  

Layering is especially useful when you want a heading to sit on top of a background image or a button to overlay a video thumbnail.

### Grouping and Aligning  

1. Hold **Shift** and click each element you want to treat as a set.  
2. Right‑click and choose **Group**.  

A grouped object can be moved, resized, and aligned as a single unit.  

- Use the **Align** icons (top, middle, bottom, left, center, right) to line up elements precisely.  
- The **Distribute** tool spreads multiple objects evenly across a space.  

---

## Saving, Previewing, and Publishing Changes  

- **Save** frequently (the **Save** button appears at the top‑right).  
- Click **Preview** to view the page as visitors will see it; this mode also shows how interactive widgets behave.  
- When you’re satisfied, click **Publish** (or **Update Site** if already published) to push changes live.  

If you need to revert a recent change, use the **Undo** button (or **Ctrl + Z**) or open the **Site History** from the Wix Dashboard to restore a previous version.

---

## Key Takeaways  

- **Text elements**: Insert a Text Box, use proper heading hierarchy (H1‑H3), and fine‑tune typography through the Design panel.  
- **Images**: Upload via Media Manager, edit with built‑in tools, and always add alt text for accessibility and SEO.  
- **Galleries**: Choose a layout that matches your visual story, customize spacing and hover effects, and ensure responsiveness on mobile.  
- **Videos**: Embed YouTube/Vimeo links, control autoplay/loop settings, and style the player to blend with your design.  
- **Interactive widgets**: Access the Wix App Market to add contact forms, social feeds, and maps; configure each app’s settings and styling to fit your site.  
- **Styling & layering**: Use the Design panel, arrange element order, group related items, and align them for a polished look.  
- **Workflow**: Save often, preview in both desktop and mobile modes, and publish when ready, knowing you can revert via Site History if needed.  

With these tools at your fingertips, you can transform a bare‑bones page into an engaging, information‑rich experience—just like Sweet Crumbs’ vibrant online showcase. Happy designing!

modules.title: Design Basics: Themes, Colors, and Fonts
modules.content:
## Choosing a Preset Theme  

Imagine you’ve just created a Wix site for a boutique coffee shop. The owner loves the vibe of a modern, minimalist coffee house but the site still looks like a blank canvas. The fastest way to give the site personality is to **apply a preset theme** – a collection of colors, fonts, and layout styles that Wix bundles together.

1. **Open the Wix Editor** (you already did this in *Understanding the Wix Editor Interface*).  
2. Click the **“Design”** button on the left‑hand toolbar.  
3. Select **“Theme Manager.”** Here you’ll see a gallery of ready‑made themes such as *Elegant*, *Bold*, *Playful*, and *Minimalist*.  

When you hover over a theme, Wix shows a live preview of how your current page would look with that theme applied. Pick the one that best matches the coffee shop’s brand personality – for our scenario, *Minimalist* works well.

> **Tip:** Choosing a theme does **not** lock you into every element it contains. You can later tweak colors, fonts, and spacing while keeping the overall look consistent.

Once you click **“Apply”**, the theme instantly updates all pages you’ve built so far, giving you a cohesive visual foundation to work from.

---

## Modifying the Theme Palette  

A **palette** is the set of colors the theme uses for backgrounds, text, buttons, and accents. Changing the palette lets you align the site with the brand’s specific colors (e.g., the coffee shop’s deep brown and creamy ivory).

### Where to Find the Palette  

1. In the **Theme Manager**, click **“Colors.”**  
2. You’ll see a row of color swatches labeled *Primary*, *Secondary*, *Accent*, and *Background*.  

### Editing a Swatch  

- Click any swatch. A color picker appears with three ways to choose a new hue:  
  * **Palette grid** – a set of popular colors.  
  * **Hex code field** – type a precise web color code (e.g., `#4B2E2A`).  
  * **RGB sliders** – adjust red, green, and blue values manually.  

> **Jargon note:** A **hex code** is a six‑character code that represents a specific color on the web. It always starts with a `#`.

### Practical Example  

The coffee shop’s logo uses **#4B2E2A** for the beans and **#F5EEDC** for the cream background.

- Change the **Primary** swatch to `#4B2E2A`.  
- Change the **Background** swatch to `#F5EEDC`.  

All elements that previously used the generic “Primary” color (like button backgrounds and heading highlights) now adopt the new deep‑brown tone, instantly tying the site to the brand.

### Saving and Naming Your Palette  

After adjusting the colors, click **“Save As New Palette.”** Give it a descriptive name like *CoffeeShop‑Brand*. You can switch between saved palettes later, which is handy if you experiment with seasonal color schemes.

---

## Setting Global Fonts  

A **global font** is a typeface applied automatically to all text elements that inherit the theme’s typography settings. Using global fonts ensures that headings, paragraphs, and menus look harmonious without you having to edit each text box individually.

### Accessing Font Settings  

1. From **Theme Manager**, select **“Fonts.”**  
2. You’ll see three categories: *Headings*, *Paragraphs*, and *Buttons*.  

### Choosing a Font  

Wix offers three ways to pick a font:

- **Wix Font Library** – a curated list of free web‑safe fonts (e.g., *Montserrat*, *Lora*).  
- **Google Fonts** – thousands of open‑source fonts you can preview instantly.  
- **Upload Your Own** – if you have a brand‑specific font file (usually `.woff` or `.ttf`), you can upload it for exclusive use.  

For the coffee shop, a clean sans‑serif like **Montserrat** works well for headings, while a softer serif such as **Lora** gives body text an inviting feel.

### Applying the Fonts  

- Click the **Headings** dropdown → select *Montserrat*.  
- Click the **Paragraphs** dropdown → select *Lora*.  
- For **Buttons**, you can either keep the heading font or choose a third option that matches your brand’s tone.  

All existing headings and paragraphs instantly update. New text boxes you add later will automatically inherit these choices.

### Adjusting Individual Element Styles  

Sometimes a specific element needs a different look—perhaps the hero tagline should be in a handwritten script to convey a cozy, artisanal vibe.

1. **Select the text element** on the canvas.  
2. In the floating toolbar, click the **“Edit Text”** icon (the pencil).  
3. The **Text Settings** panel appears on the right. Here you can override the global font, size, color, and line height **just for this element**.  

> **Best practice:** Keep overrides to a minimum. Over‑customizing individual elements breaks the visual consistency that the theme provides.

---

## Fine‑Tuning Font Details  

Beyond the typeface itself, you can adjust **size**, **weight**, **letter spacing**, and **line height**—the spacing between letters and lines of text. These settings affect readability and visual hierarchy.

| Setting | What It Controls | Typical Use |
|---------|------------------|-------------|
| **Size** | Height of the characters | Larger for headings, smaller for body copy |
| **Weight** | Thickness of the stroke (e.g., Light, Regular, Bold) | Bold for emphasis, Light for subtlety |
| **Letter spacing** | Space between individual characters | Wider spacing for uppercase logos |
| **Line height** | Space between lines of text | Higher line height improves readability on long paragraphs |

To adjust these globally:

1. In **Theme Manager → Fonts**, click the **gear icon** next to a font category.  
2. A modal appears where you can set default size, weight, etc.  

If you need a unique look for a single button, repeat the steps under *Adjusting Individual Element Styles*.

---

## Using Spacing Tools to Align and Distribute Elements  

Consistent spacing is a silent hero of good design. Wix provides several **spacing tools** that help you line up elements and create even gaps, making the page feel organized and professional.

### 1. The Snap Grid  

When you drag an element, thin pink lines appear, indicating **snap points**—pre‑defined positions where the element will automatically align with other objects on the page.  

- **Enable/disable** the snap grid via **“Settings → Snap to Grid”** in the editor’s top bar.  
- **Snap to Guides** lets you create custom invisible lines (click the ruler at the top/left, drag a guide onto the canvas).  

### 2. Alignment Buttons  

Select multiple elements (hold **Shift** while clicking each one) and a small toolbar appears with icons for:

- **Align Left / Center / Right** – aligns selected elements along the chosen edge.  
- **Align Top / Middle / Bottom** – aligns vertically.  

For the coffee shop homepage, you might select the logo, navigation menu, and a call‑to‑action button, then click **Align Bottom** so they sit on the same horizontal line.

### 3. Distribute (Even Spacing)  

After aligning, you often need equal gaps between elements. With the same multiple‑selection active:

- Click the **Distribute Horizontally** icon to create uniform horizontal spacing.  
- Click **Distribute Vertically** for equal vertical gaps.  

These tools are especially handy in sections like a *Featured Products* grid where each product card should have the same distance from its neighbors.

### 4. Padding and Margin  

**Padding** is the space **inside** an element’s border (e.g., the space between a button’s edge and its text). **Margin** is the space **outside** the element (e.g., the gap between a button and the surrounding image).  

To edit these:

1. Click an element and open the **Design** panel (paint‑brush icon).  
2. Choose **“Spacing.”**  
3. Adjust sliders for **Top/Bottom/Left/Right Padding** and **Margin**.  

For a button that feels cramped, increase its **Horizontal Padding** by 10 px. For a section where text feels too close to the edge of the page, add **Bottom Margin** to push the next element down.

### 5. Using the “Strip” Container for Consistent Layout  

A **strip** is a full‑width container you can place multiple elements inside. Strips have their own spacing controls, making them ideal for building repeatable sections (e.g., a three‑column testimonial area).

- Add a strip via **Add → Strip → Blank Strip**.  
- Drag your text boxes and images into the strip.  
- Use the strip’s **Layout** options to set **“Column Gap”** (the space between columns) and **“Content Padding.”**  

All elements inside the strip automatically respect these settings, reducing the need to adjust each piece individually.

---

## Bringing It All Together: A Walkthrough  

Let’s walk through the entire process for our coffee shop site, from theme selection to final spacing polish.

1. **Apply a Theme** – Choose *Minimalist* in Theme Manager → *Apply*.  
2. **Customize the Palette** – Change Primary to `#4B2E2A` (deep brown) and Background to `#F5EEDC` (cream). Save as *CoffeeShop‑Brand*.  
3. **Set Global Fonts** – Headings → *Montserrat*, Paragraphs → *Lora*. Adjust global size: Headings 36 px, Paragraphs 18 px.  
4. **Override Hero Tagline** – Select the hero text, change the font to *Pacifico* (handwritten), increase size to 48 px, set color to Primary (deep brown).  
5. **Align Navigation** – Select logo, menu, and “Order Now” button → Align Bottom → Distribute Horizontally.  
6. **Create a Product Strip** – Add a blank strip, insert three product cards, set Column Gap to 30 px, add 20 px Bottom Padding to each card.  
7. **Fine‑Tune Spacing** – For the “About Us” section, increase Bottom Margin of the heading by 15 px to give breathing room before the paragraph.  

When you preview the site (click **Preview** at the top right), the changes are instantly visible. The site now feels cohesive: colors match the logo, fonts reinforce the brand tone, and elements are neatly aligned and evenly spaced.

---

## Troubleshooting Common Issues  

| Problem | Likely Cause | Quick Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----------|
| **Colors don’t update everywhere** | Some elements have **custom color overrides** (e.g., a button you manually colored). | Select the element → **Design → Color** → click **Reset to Theme**. |
| **Text looks different on mobile** | Mobile view has its own **font size scaling**. | Switch to **Mobile Editor** (bottom toolbar) → adjust font sizes separately or enable **“Sync with Desktop”** for fonts. |
| **Elements jump out of alignment after editing** | Snap grid was turned off, or margin/padding values conflict. | Re‑enable **Snap to Grid**, then use **Align** and **Distribute** tools again. |
| **Uploaded font not showing** | The font file isn’t web‑compatible (e.g., missing `@font-face` definitions). | Use a **Wix‑approved** `.woff` file or choose a similar Google Font instead. |

---

## Best Practices for Brand Consistency  

- **Limit the palette**: Stick to 2–3 primary colors plus neutrals. Too many hues dilute brand identity.  
- **Choose complementary fonts**: Pair a sans‑serif with a serif or a handwritten script, but avoid using more than three different typefaces.  
- **Use spacing deliberately**: Consistent padding and margins create a rhythm that users subconsciously trust.  
- **Document your decisions**: Keep a simple style sheet (e.g., a Google Doc) listing your palette hex codes, chosen fonts, and spacing values. This becomes a reference for future pages or team members.  

---

## Going Beyond the Basics (Optional Exploration)  

If you feel comfortable after mastering the preset theme workflow, you can:

- **Create a custom theme from scratch**: In Theme Manager, click **“Create New Theme”** and build your palette and fonts without starting from a preset.  
- **Add animation to elements**: Use the **“Animation”** panel to give hover or entrance effects, but keep them subtle to preserve readability.  
- **Set up a style guide page**: Dedicate a hidden page in your site that lists your brand’s colors, fonts, and spacing rules for future reference.  

These steps are not required for the current learning objectives but can further elevate the professionalism of your Wix site.

---

## Recap of Tools Covered  

- **Theme Manager** – Apply themes, edit palettes, set global fonts.  
- **Color Picker** – Hex codes, palette grid, RGB sliders.  
- **Font Settings** – Global categories, individual overrides, weight & spacing options.  
- **Spacing Toolbox** – Snap grid, alignment buttons, distribute icons, padding/margin sliders.  
- **Strips** – Container for repeatable, evenly spaced layouts.  

By mastering these tools, you can transform any Wix template into a polished, brand‑aligned website with minimal effort.

## Key Takeaways  

- **Preset themes give you an instant visual foundation**; you can still customize every color and font afterward.  
- **A palette is more than a set of colors**—it defines how those colors appear across backgrounds, text, and UI elements. Use hex codes for precise brand matching.  
- **Global fonts ensure typographic consistency**, while occasional element‑level overrides let you add personality where needed.  
- **Spacing tools (snap grid, alignment, distribution, padding, margin, strips) keep your layout tidy and professional**; use them early to avoid “messy” designs later.  
- **Save and name your custom palettes and font sets** so you can quickly switch between brand variations (e.g., seasonal themes).  
- **Document your design decisions** to maintain brand consistency as your site grows or as collaborators join the project.

modules.title: Mobile Optimization
modules.content:
## A Phone‑First Reality Check  

Imagine you’ve just launched a fresh Wix site for your boutique coffee shop. You share the link with a friend, and she opens it on her iPhone while waiting in line. The beautiful hero image you set on the desktop stretches off‑screen, the navigation menu is hidden behind a tiny icon, and the “Call Now” button she needs to place an order doesn’t work at all. She’s impressed by the design on a laptop, but on her phone the experience feels clunky—and she quickly taps away.

That moment is a common wake‑up call for beginners: a site that looks perfect on a desktop can fall apart on a mobile device. Since more than half of global web traffic now arrives from smartphones and tablets, **mobile optimization** isn’t a nice‑to‑have; it’s essential. In Wix, you can fine‑tune the mobile version of your site without starting from scratch. Let’s walk through the process step by step.

---

## Switching to Mobile View  

### 1. Open the Wix Editor  

If you’re still on the **Wix Editor** after completing the earlier modules (Choosing a Template, Adding Content, etc.), you’re already where you need to be.  

1. Log in at **www.wix.com** and select **My Sites**.  
2. Click **Edit Site** for the project you want to work on.  

### 2. Locate the Mobile Icon  

At the top toolbar of the editor, you’ll see two small icons side by side:

- **Desktop View** (the default)  
- **Mobile View** (a phone silhouette)

> **Tip:** The icons look like a computer monitor and a smartphone. Hovering over them displays a tooltip that reads “Switch to Mobile”.

Click the **Mobile View** icon. Wix instantly reloads the editor, showing a preview of how your site will appear on a typical smartphone screen (around 375 px wide).  

> **Note:** You are now in a **mobile‑only editing mode**. Any changes you make here affect only the mobile version; the desktop layout remains unchanged.

### 3. Understand the Mobile Editing Panel  

When in Mobile View, a new panel slides in from the right side labeled **Mobile Settings**. Here you can:

- Turn **Hide on Mobile** on/off for any element  
- Adjust **Mobile Menu** options  
- Enable **Tap‑to‑Call** for phone numbers  

Familiarize yourself with this panel—most of the mobile‑specific controls live here.

---

## How Mobile View Differs From Desktop View  

### 1. Stacked Layout
